title: Time-to-reach benchmark
description: Single source of truth for one benchmark. Semantics: with s = +1 for direction 'forward' (default) and s = -1 for 'backward', the benchmark is 'reachable' iff there exist x0 in the union of initial_sets and t in [time_horizon[0], time_horizon[1]] such that the solution x(t) of dx/dt = s*f(x), x(0) = x0, lies in the union of target_sets. A backward problem therefore follows the time-reversed flow of f from initial_sets. State variables are named x1..xn.

id.description: Benchmark identifier; equals the file name without .json.

notes.description: Free-form remarks that matter for interpreting results.

equations.description: Right-hand side f_i(x1..xn) for i = 1..n; '^' and '**' both denote powers. May use the names in 'parameters' and 'definitions'.

parameters.description: Named constants (e.g. masses, feedback gains), substituted into 'definitions' and 'equations'.

definitions.description: Named sub-expressions (e.g. a control law u), in order: each may use the states, the parameters and earlier definitions.

direction.description: 'forward': trajectories of dx/dt = f(x). 'backward': trajectories of the time-reversed system dx/dt = -f(x), i.e. backward reachability from initial_sets. 'system' always states the forward vector field f.

domain.description: Axis-aligned box that contains every initial set, every target set and all trajectories from the initial sets over the time horizon. Grid- and region-based tools use it as their computational domain.

dims.description: Pairs of 0-based state indices to plot.

oneOf.description: Axis-aligned box; lower == upper is allowed (degenerate dimension).
{x in bounding_box : function(x) <= 0}. The bounding box must enclose the sublevel set's relevant component; tools that cannot handle level sets may use the box as an outer approximation.
